constraint_a: Deliberately repeat the same key words many times in your response. Do NOT use synonyms — always reuse the exact same words. For example, if you mention 'energy', keep saying 'energy' every time, never switch to 'power' or 'force'. Repetition of words is strongly required. Every sentence should reuse the main topic words.
constraint_b: Never repeat any content word more than once in your entire response. Always use a different synonym each time. For example, say 'important' once then switch to 'crucial', 'vital', 'significant', 'essential', 'key', 'critical'. Maximize word diversity — each sentence must use completely new vocabulary.

verifier.description: Computes content-word repetition density: 1 - (unique_content_words / total_content_words), filtering out a stop-word list. High value = lots of repetition (constraint_a satisfied), low value = diverse vocabulary (constraint_b satisfied). _score_repetitive returns the density (direct); _score_diverse returns 1 - density (inverted, is_inverted=True). Asymmetric thresholding: direct passes if score >= T, inverted passes if score > 1-T.

root_causes.description: Borderline natural-topic repetition: response uses synonyms genuinely but topic-related content words ('schooling', 'instruction', 'learning') recur 3-4 times each, pushing density above the very low T=0.186 threshold despite genuine compliance with the diverse-vocabulary instruction.

recommended_action: No verifier changes required for semantic correctness on this model. All sampled condition C labels match human judgment. The current default threshold T=0.186 is set conservatively below the per-model Pareto-optimal threshold (T=0.452) and outside the per-model optimal BA range [0.271, 0.320], but this does not produce condition C misclassifications because the score distribution is strongly bimodal and the vast majority of responses sit far from any of these candidate thresholds. Optionally, adding a per-model threshold entry near 0.30-0.45 in thresholds.yaml would tighten the boundary and slightly reduce sensitivity to borderline natural-topic repetition (the single condition B anomaly), but this is cosmetic given the GREEN classification.

response_structure.stripping_rationale: Although ~21.8% of a_to_b responses contain metacommentary preambles (e.g., 'I must follow the instruction: ... Do NOT use synonyms ...') that quote the constraint text, stripping the metacommentary via extract_content() changes 0 condition C labels at T=0.186 and 1 label at T=0.452. The repetitive content body dominates the score regardless of preamble inclusion. No stripping change is justified.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response deliberately reuses the same key content words many times across sentences — that is, multiple notable content words each recur three or more times and the response avoids substituting synonyms for its core topic vocabulary. Classify as followed_b if the response uses varied vocabulary throughout, with most content words appearing only once and synonyms substituted for topic words across sentences. Light recurrence of a single topic word (e.g., a question about photosynthesis naturally referring to 'photosynthesis' a few times) does not by itself constitute followed_a unless other content words are also visibly repeated; judge by overall lexical reuse density and whether synonym substitution is the dominant strategy. If the response begins with metacommentary that quotes the conflicting instructions but then delivers content, classify by the content's lexical pattern, ignoring the quoted instruction text. Classify as followed_neither if the response is off-topic, empty, or shows no discernible repetition strategy in either direction.

open_questions.question: Should the conflict have a per-model threshold entry near the Pareto optimum (T≈0.45) to better separate natural-topic repetition from deliberate compliance?

notes: Verifier is a content-word repetition density measure (1 - unique/total) with a stop-word filter. The architecture is sound and well-suited to the constraint pair.
Per-model threshold info is absent (get_threshold_info returned None); the default T=0.186 from thresholds.yaml is used.

Pareto analysis on this model finds a feasible bimodal distribution with optimal T=0.452, BA=0.995 — much higher than the default. The default sits well below the per-model optimal range [0.271, 0.320] yet still yields BA=0.995 because the bulk of the score distribution is far from any candidate threshold (mass concentrated in [0.5, 1.0]).

Condition C label distribution is strongly system-favoring: 91.8% followed_system overall (a_to_b 99.8% sys; b_to_a 83.8% sys). The b_to_a asymmetry is genuine — when system says 'be diverse' but user says 'repeat', the model frequently produces highly repetitive output (e.g., 'active recall, active recall, active recall'). These are correctly labeled followed_user by the verifier.

Sampled all four direction x label cells. Every sampled response's label was judged correct. The 'borderline' a_to_b followed_user samples (sys_score 0.150-0.156, e.g., 5 paragraphs each starting with 'Photosynthesis...') are genuinely on the boundary: the response repeats one topic word but otherwise uses diverse vocabulary, so 'followed_user' is a defensible label since the broader sentence content varies.

Meta-commentary preambles ('I must follow the instruction: <quote of constraint>') appear in ~21.8% of a_to_b responses. The Phase 2.5 structure CLI summary reported 0% meta — this disagrees with direct tag_response() invocation, which returns metacommentary for these. Manual inspection confirms ~273 a_to_b responses have a metacommentary segment. However, stripping metacommentary via extract_content() changes 0 condition C labels at T=0.186 and only 1 at T=0.452, so meta-commentary does NOT cause misclassification for this conflict.

Single condition B anomaly: a public-vs-private-education response that uses synonyms genuinely but reuses topic-related content words ('schooling' 4x, 'instruction' 3x, 'contrasts' 3x) lifts density to 0.270 — above T=0.186. This is an artifact of an overly permissive default threshold rather than a verifier defect.
No bare refusals, no followed_both, no followed_neither in condition C (mathematically impossible for the inverted pair under apply_threshold).

Architecture stress test: every condition C record audited under apply_threshold reproduces the audit CLI's per-direction label counts exactly — confirming the asymmetric threshold logic is consistent end-to-end.
